extracted.intended_audience: K-12 educators, district leaders, state and national policy-makers, and researchers interested in STEM education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for defining, identifying, and supporting highly successful K-12 STEM schools and programs, including criteria, recommended practices, and policy-level actions to improve STEM outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge: outline criteria for identifying effective STEM schools/programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee was charged with 'outlining criteria for identifying effective STEM schools and programs and identifying which of these criteria could be addressed with available data and research, and those where further work is needed to develop appropriate data sources.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This framing requires criteria that are evidence-based where possible, and an explicit assessment of data availability and research gaps; the committee's work should separate criteria that can be measured with existing data from those requiring new data-development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the adoption of STEM-focused schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Districts seeking to improve STEM outcomes should consider the adoption of STEM-focused schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report identifies three models for such schools (see guidance entry): selective STEM schools for academically talented students who need to apply for admission; inclusive STEM high schools often referred to as 'magnet schools'; and schools and programs with STEM-focused career and technical education. Districts should weigh which model fits local goals and equity considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models of STEM-focused schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Three recommended models: selective STEM schools, inclusive STEM high schools ('magnet schools'), and schools/programs with STEM-focused career and technical education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as distinct organizational approaches districts can adopt; choice of model affects access, student composition, and implementation strategies and should be considered when identifying or designing 'highly successful' STEM programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devote adequate instructional time and resources to science in grades K-5
rubrics_metrics.description: Districts should devote adequate instructional time and resources to science in grades K-5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EarlyElementary science exposure is highlighted as essential; adequacy implies scheduling time, providing materials, and staffing to support meaningful science learning in primary grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure STEM curricula are focused, rigorous, and articulated
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that STEM curricula are focused on the most important topics in each discipline, are rigorous, and are articulated as a sequence of topics and performances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum quality is defined not just by content coverage but by prioritization of key disciplinary ideas, cognitive rigor, and coherent sequencing across grades with clearly defined performances/learning progressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance the capacity of K-12 teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance the capacity of K-12 teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improving teacher capacity encompasses subject-matter knowledge, pedagogical skill, and supports (e.g., professional development, coaching, resources) needed to teach rigorous STEM curricula effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide professional development for instructional leaders to create supportive school conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructional leaders with professional development that helps them create the school conditions that appear to support student achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership PD should target building school-level conditions (culture, resource allocation, scheduling, teacher collaboration structures) shown to support student STEM achievement and successful implementation of STEM programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate science to same level as reading and mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational organizations and policymakers at the state and national levels should elevate science to the same level of importance as reading and mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and accountability frameworks, resource allocation, standards adoption, and curricular emphasis should reflect science's parity with other core subjects to signal its importance and drive systemic support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop assessments aligned with next-generation science standards emphasizing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop effective systems of assessment that are aligned with the next generation of science standards and that emphasize science practices rather than mere factual recall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment systems should measure students' ability to engage in science practices (e.g., inquiry, explanation, modeling) and align with curricular goals and standards, moving beyond multiple-choice factual recall toward performance- and practice-based measures where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in coherent, focused, and sustained support for STEM teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in a coherent, focused, and sustained set of support for STEM teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained investments include long-term professional learning systems, mentoring/coaching, curricular resources, and structures that maintain and scale teacher capacity-building rather than short-term workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support key areas for future research
rubrics_metrics.description: Support key areas for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers and funders should invest in research to address gaps identified by the committee—e.g., measuring program effectiveness, scalability, data-development for new criteria—and prioritize studies that inform policy and practice for identifying and scaling successful STEM programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop objectives for assessing successful STEM education
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop aimed to identify a range of goals for highly successful STEM education; explore criteria for identifying success relative to those goals; classify strategies and educational practices schools/districts use; and identify scalable best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process-oriented rubric suggests evaluators should (1) define success goals explicitly, (2) select criteria tied to those goals, (3) map strategies/practices to outcomes, and (4) assess scalability and evidence base when judging programs.
